senses.gloss:
Koṇārka
------------------------------------------
Koṇārka (also spelt as Konārak), is about 30 kms. (20 miles) to the north-east of the well-known place of पिल्ग्रिमगे पुरी or Jagannāthapurī, in the Orissa State on the east coast. It is famous for the wonderful temple of सूर्य (Sun-god), now in ruins. It has been built resembling a रथ or a chariot a replica of the रथ in which सूर्य travels in the sky all-round the earth. Legends attribute its entire concept and design to the vision of an expert sculptor विष्णु-mahārāṇa.
कोणार्क">Sūrya Temple at KoṇārkaThe whole temple is in the नागर style, peculiar to Kaliṅgadeśa or the present-day Orissa.
The temple was built by the king Narasiṁhadeva of the Gaṅga dynasty in the 13th century A. D. He is said to have ruled from A. D. 1238 to 1264.
As per one account, twelve thousand workers are said to have toiled for twelve long years to build this temple.
This temple, conceived as the gigantic solar chariot has twelve pairs of exquisitely carved wheels, each 3 metres (10 ft.) in diameter. It is drawn by seven steeds.
The sanctum, now, has no roof nor the image. The nāṭmandir (the nṛtta-मण्डप or dance-hall) also has no roof.
The jagmohan (ardhamaṇḍapa) which is almost intact measures 34.15 metres (114 ft.) square and the total height of the शिखर is 38.4 metres (128 ft.).
The whole temple is on a raised platform.
The sanctum has 3 superb images of the Sun-god in the three cardinal niches, shown as projecting subsidiary shrines. The walls of the jagmohan are adorned with geometric motifs, people, mythical animals and erotic scenes.
There is an iron beam below the roof of the jagmohan, 6 metres (20 ft.) long and 24 cms. (about 10 inches) in thickness. Its weight had been estimated to be 61 tonnes!
Symbolically speaking, the 24 wheels represent the 24 pakṣas or fortnights in a year. The seven horses stand for the seven colours in the sunlight, generally indicated by the word VIBGYOR.
